reason: The hypothesis relies on general thermomechanical processing benefits shown in a different alloy (CoCrNi MEA, E3) and on grain-boundary stability/residual stress concepts from a nanocrystalline HEA film (E2), but none of the cited evidence involves the target MM'X-type magnetocaloric alloy or demonstrates preservation of caloric response after such processing. The key premise that caloric performance is maintained is entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Thermomechanical processing (warm deformation + annealing) refines grain structure in HEAs/MEAs.
Grain refinement and reduced residual stresses enhance compressive strength and ductility.
Microstructural refinement does not degrade the caloric phase transformation response.
The cited evidence on CoCrNi MEA and HEA films is transferable to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy system.
